headline: GOLD BREAKS $4,000 AS PCE INFLATION HITS 3.6% — Silver Slumps to Fresh 2026 Low Near $51 on December Hike Lock-In
snippet: The September PCE inflation report (headline 3.6%, core 3.1%) released October 29 cemented December rate-hike expectations above 80% and drove spot gold briefly below $4,000 intraday on October 30 — its first sustained breach since July. Silver extended its losing streak to a third consecutive day, hitting a fresh 2026 low near $51.00 and down 11.9% on the week. The SPDR Gold Shares ETF shed 2.0% while the iShares Silver Trust fell 6.0%, as both metals face compounding headwinds: a hawkish Fed, a stronger dollar, and silver's additional exposure to slowing industrial demand.

headline: EVOLUTION MINING SEALS A$213M CARNABY COPPER SCHEME TODAY — Greater Duchess Queensland Asset to Feed Ernest Henry Mill
snippet: Evolution Mining's (ASX: EVN) A$213 million all-share acquisition of Carnaby Resources (ASX: CNB) takes effect October 30, following Supreme Court of Western Australia approval on October 29. The deal adds Carnaby's Greater Duchess copper project in north-west Queensland — 29 million tonnes at 1.5% copper equivalent, containing 441,000 tonnes of copper equivalent metal — to Evolution's portfolio. The strategic rationale is using latent capacity at the Ernest Henry copper-gold mine in Cloncurry to process Greater Duchess ore without incremental capital for a standalone processing facility.

headline: KINROSS Q3 REVENUE MISSES BY $190M, STOCK FALLS 5% — Output Down 16% YoY to 424,693 oz Despite EPS Beat
snippet: Kinross Gold (TSX: K) reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.77 billion, missing FactSet estimates of $1.96 billion by roughly $190 million, as attributable gold-equivalent production fell 16% year-on-year to 424,693 ounces. Adjusted EPS of $0.50 per share beat consensus by about $0.02, but the revenue shortfall drove the stock down 5.03% to $21.83 in after-hours trading on October 28. The company maintained its updated full-year guidance and said operations remain on track. The miss adds Kinross to the list of senior gold producers whose Q3 output disappointed, pressured by a challenging operational environment across the sector.

headline: GLENCORE Q3: COBALT SINKS 52% AS DRC QUOTAS BITE — Mutanda Zero, Copper Falls Short of Consensus, Full-Year at Low End
snippet: Glencore's Q3 2026 production report released October 29 showed own-sourced cobalt output collapsing 52% year-on-year to 13,700 tonnes in the first nine months, with Mutanda — historically one of the world's largest cobalt mines — reporting zero cobalt production as the DRC export quota regime throttles output. Copper fared better in absolute terms (598,600 tonnes nine-month, up 3% YoY), but Glencore trimmed full-year copper guidance to the low end of its 810–870 kt range, missing analyst consensus by about 4%. The cobalt supply squeeze, driven by DRC quotas that run at least through 2027, continues to structurally tighten the battery raw material market.

headline: CENTRAL ASIA METALS CLOSES A$232M CYGNUS DEAL — TSX Listing Won, Chibougamau Copper-Gold Joins Portfolio
snippet: Central Asia Metals (AIM: CAML) completed its all-share acquisition of Cygnus Metals on October 27, issuing 78.5 million new shares in a deal valued at approximately A$232 million. The transaction brings Cygnus's flagship Chibougamau copper-gold project in Québec — which has not yet reached a development decision — into CAML's portfolio. CAML simultaneously secured a new Toronto Stock Exchange listing alongside its existing AIM presence, giving the company access to North American capital markets. Former Cygnus managing director Ernest Mast joins the CAML board as independent non-executive director.

headline: PPX MINING HITS 5,204 g/t SILVER AND 13 g/t GOLD OVER 1m IN PERU — Callanquitas Bonanza Zone Open at Depth
snippet: PPX Mining (TSXV: PPX) reported drill hole CA-26-35 at its Callanquitas gold-silver-copper project in Peru, returning a bonanza-grade interval of 13.28 g/t gold, 5,204 g/t silver and 5.4% copper over 1.0 metre within a broader zone of 20.85 metres at 1.35 g/t gold and 16.10 g/t silver. Mineralisation remains open to the north and at depth across both zones in the Callanquitas East structure, and the company also completed its first drill hole at the adjacent Portachuelos target, expanding the footprint of an emerging polymetallic system in a district historically known for high-grade epithermal mineralisation.

headline: GOLD FALLS EVEN AS THE DOLLAR AND YIELDS DROP — FXStreet Flags Cross-Asset Deleveraging as Culprit Behind Anomalous Move
snippet: An October 29 FXStreet analysis highlighted an unusual disconnect: gold futures fell despite a simultaneous drop in the US dollar and Treasury yields — the opposite of gold's historically reliable inverse relationship with the greenback. The author attributes the anomaly to forced cross-asset liquidation, noting that equities and crypto sold off in parallel and arguing this reflects deleveraging pressure rather than fundamental gold selling. December gold futures tested the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement near $4,097 before reversing lower, suggesting that near-term resistance is technically intact even if the underlying bid is temporarily overwhelmed.

headline: SILVER BEARS EYE $48 AS RSI HITS OVERSOLD — 78.6% Fibo Retracement Marks Next Major Floor if $51 Gives Way
snippet: An FX Empire technical analysis flags the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement of silver's April 2025 advance at $48.29 as the next significant target if the $51.00 floor gives way — a level not tested since 2024. With RSI entering oversold territory on daily charts and Fed December hike odds above 80%, the analysis argues silver faces compounding pressure from both the monetary policy headwind (non-yielding asset in a rising-rate environment) and an industrial demand slowdown (more than half of silver's demand comes from industrial end-uses). A recovery above $54.00 would be the first technical evidence of seller exhaustion.

headline: TRIFECTA GOLD DELIVERS 2026 RYE ASSAYS — Tombstone Belt Yukon System Returns Gold and Polymetallic Zones
snippet: Trifecta Gold (TSXV: TG) released assay results from its six-hole, 1,852-metre 2026 drill program at the Rye Project in the Tombstone Gold Belt, Yukon, with holes returning a gold zone and a separate copper-silver zone among the intercepts. The 2025 Rye program had produced standout intervals including 44.3 g/t gold over 0.58 m and 1,465 g/t silver over 1.97 m in prior holes at the polymetallic system. Rye is one of several active targets for Trifecta in the Tombstone Belt — a district that has generated multiple multi-million-ounce gold discoveries since 2020, including Coffee, Goldstrike, and White Gold.

headline: BTU METALS SPUDS FIRST HOLES AT HUBCAP, WAWA — 1,200-Metre Program Targets Gold Adjacent to Red Pine's 17 g/t War Eagle Zone
snippet: BTU Metals (TSXV: BTU) commenced its initial 1,200-metre drill program at the Hubcap gold property near Wawa, Ontario, testing high-priority geophysical and surface targets across 5–7 holes. The property boundary sits 700 metres from Red Pine Exploration's War Eagle zone, which returned assays up to 17.1 g/t gold, and historical surface sampling at Hubcap has reached 6 g/t. The Wawa gold district in northern Ontario has seen renewed junior activity as infrastructure improvements lower exploration costs in a belt with confirmed multi-gram gold mineralisation across multiple systems.
